title: 2048-context regression: epoch sweep, control, and guard efficacy
summary: Two questions, one answered decisively and one NOT answered. (1) GUARD EFFICACY: the chat-template windowing guard (5-message cap) prevents the growing-conversation KV-cache crash BY ITSELF at 512 context -- 14 turns, zero crashes, prompt_tokens plateauing at ~102 while messages sent grew to 27, against a hard crash at turn 3 without it. The 2048 context raise was therefore unnecessary. (2) WHY 2048 DEGRADED Q&A: NOT ANSWERED. The epoch-inflation hypothesis was tested by this sweep and is NOT supported -- termination is non-monotone across 0.74-4.00 epochs and every comparison against the 512 control is NOT SIGNIFICANT at n=32. The metrics chosen (termination rate, type/token ratio) do not discriminate these models at all; what discriminates is Q&A coherence, which was read rather than scored.
instrument_limitations: n=32 sampled completions per checkpoint -- underpowered for proportions near 0.1 (binomial SE ~0.05), which is why every pairwise comparison lands NOT SIGNIFICANT.

Termination measured on 4 story prompts x 8 samples, NOT this project's frozen prompt set B, so these numbers are NOT comparable to score_behaviour.py's published termination figures (0.0542/0.0250). Within-sweep comparison is valid; cross-instrument comparison is not.
Type/token ratio is flat (0.707-0.741) across every checkpoint including the control -- it carries no signal here and should not be cited as evidence in either direction.
The 512-vs-2048 comparison is CONFOUNDED: those runs differ in seq_len AND epochs (1.00 vs 4.00) simultaneously. This data cannot separate them.

guard_efficacy.condition: episod/tt-tnt-1024 served at --max_model_len 512 (the exact crash condition), chat template active from tokenizer_config.json
guard_efficacy.verdict: guard alone is sufficient; context raise unnecessary
